title: Transforming Values: map, tap, and scan

questions.prompt: `of(1, 2, 3).pipe(scan((acc, n) => acc + n, 0))` emits which sequence?
questions.explanation: scan emits the running accumulator after each value: 0+1=1, 1+2=3, 3+3=6. (reduce would emit only the final 6, and only on completion.)

questions.prompt: What effect does `tap` have on the values passing through it?

options.text: None — values pass through unchanged; tap only runs side effects
It transforms each value by its return value

questions.explanation: tap performs side effects (logging, analytics, DOM writes) and forwards every value untouched. To transform, use map.

questions.prompt: Why does `interval(1000).pipe(reduce((a, n) => a + n, 0))` never emit a value?

options.text: reduce emits only when the source completes, and interval never completes
reduce is not a valid operator on interval
reduce requires a seed of 1, not 0
interval emits strings, which reduce cannot add

questions.explanation: reduce accumulates and emits a single value on completion. Since interval is infinite, completion never happens, so reduce never emits. scan would emit a running total instead.

questions.prompt: Which practices keep transformation pipelines clean and predictable? Select all that apply.

options.text: Keep map callbacks pure (no side effects)
Return a new object/array from scan instead of mutating the accumulator
Use tap for logging and analytics
Put DOM writes and logging inside map for convenience

questions.explanation: map should be pure, scan accumulators should be immutable, and side effects belong in tap — not in map.

questions.prompt: Complete the immutable append in scan: `scan((acc, x) => [________, x], [])` (type what goes before the comma to spread the existing array).
questions.explanation: Spreading the accumulator, `[...acc, x]`, returns a new array each step instead of mutating the old one — so each emission is an independent snapshot.

questions.prompt: Match each operator to its job.

pairs.right: Run side effects without changing values
Emit a running accumulator every step
Emit one final value on completion

questions.explanation: map transforms, tap observes, scan accumulates and emits each step, and reduce accumulates and emits once when the source completes.
